correctness.rationale: A singleton level c gives an explicit pointwise-comparison contraction id <= u >= const_c. If every level has at least two points, no point has a unique strict upper minimum or strict lower maximum, so the finite space is a Stong core. Its order complex is the join D_{r_1}*...*D_{r_h}; iterating D_r*X homotopy equivalent to a wedge of r-1 suspensions of X gives the stated wedge of spheres. Homotopy-equivalent finite cores are homeomorphic, and the intrinsic incomparability classes of a weak order are exactly its linearly ordered levels, so homeomorphism preserves the ordered size vector. McCord reduces weak homotopy type to the order-complex type; positive wedges of spheres are classified here by sphere dimension h-1 and top reduced homology rank product_i(r_i-1). The frozen verifier independently stress-tests beat points, mod-2 Betti ranks and singleton contractions on several boundary examples, including W(2,4,2) versus W(2,2,4).

value.rationale: This is a complete natural classification for a standard family of finite spaces and gives a transparent family-wide answer to how much information weak homotopy forgets relative to finite-space homotopy. The explicit eight-point pair is a motivated Whitehead-type witness, while the theorem applies to all level vectors including the contractible boundary.

final_claim: For every finite weak order W(r_1,...,r_h), a singleton level makes W contractible; otherwise the order complex is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of product_i(r_i-1) spheres of dimension h-1. Two finite weak orders are ordinarily homotopy equivalent exactly when both are contractible or their ordered level-size vectors agree, while their weak homotopy types agree exactly when both are contractible or they have the same height and the same product_i(r_i-1).

The classification is for finite weak orders, not arbitrary finite posets; the weak-equivalence statement concerns weak homotopy type rather than existence of direct weak-equivalence maps in both directions.
